solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spicy food in pastry cases can lead to trouble

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the pastry dish wraps around the rest

parts.note: a pie is food baked in pastry

indicators.note: the lead to a word is its first letter, here of trouble

parts.note: T is the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A warning that spicy fillings inside pastry can cause indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE 'cases' CAN plus T (the 'lead to' trouble). 'Spicy food' reads as one phrase, but 'food in pastry' is the pie and only 'Spicy' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Picante is a Spanish-derived word for hot and sharp-tasting, as in picante sauce.

clue.text: Equips with cutlery supply in an attractive manner

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a supple or bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; 'with' joins the two words

explanation.surface: A caterer laying out knives and forks so the table looks nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun or verb meaning provision, but here it is the adverb from supple: bendily. That rare reading is the trick of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Picturesquely means in a way pretty enough to be a picture, so attractively.

clue.text: Restrict dogs

parts.note: read as a noun, a dog is a cur, a mongrel
read as a verb, to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A command to keep the dogs under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' does two jobs: as a noun it gives CUR, and as a verb (to dog someone is to tail them) it gives TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to cut it short or restrict it.

clue.text: Innocent I buried in central part of church

indicators.note: the I goes inside, covered by the other word

parts.note: the nave is the main central body of a church
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone innocent laid to rest in the middle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central part' suggests taking a middle letter, but it is a definition of NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, lacking worldly wisdom.

clue.text: Demand from alimony claim?

parts.note: alimony is claimed by an ex, a former spouse
a legal action is a claim brought in court

explanation.surface: A divorced partner's demands for money.
explanation.walkthrough: An alimony claim is an ex's action, which spells EX ACTION; the question mark flags the loose reading of 'alimony' as EX.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a demand, especially one for payment that is hard to refuse.

clue.text: Shot out of bed close to dangerous temporary installations

parts.note: a pop is a shot, as from a gun
someone out of bed is up

indicators.note: the close, or end, of 'dangerous' is taken

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone leaping out of bed near some dangerous structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot out of bed' reads as one phrase for springing awake, but it is two separate pieces: a gunshot, then being awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop-ups are temporary shops, stalls or displays set up for a short time.

clue.text: Supply weapons before war? Starmer possibly holding back

parts.note: Keir Starmer is a British Prime Minister, a PM
the back is the rear

explanation.surface: Speculation that the Prime Minister is quietly rearming ahead of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding back' reads as one phrase for restraint, but 'holding' is the container and 'back' stands alone. The question mark flags the playful definition: arming before a war.
explanation.definitionFit: To prearm is to arm in advance, so to supply weapons before the fighting starts.

clue.text: Trump is one citizen following Putin's overture

indicators.note: an overture opens a piece, so it gives the opening letter of Putin
something following comes after, so the citizen is placed after Putin's letter

parts.note: its first letter
a resident is a citizen of a place

explanation.surface: Donald Trump described as an ordinary citizen taking his lead from Putin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts RESIDENT after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is an example of a president, of the United States.

clue.text: The Now Show

definitions.meaning: a noun: this moment in time, as opposed to past or future
a verb: to display or put on view

explanation.surface: The Now Show is a long-running BBC radio comedy programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words read as one title, the BBC Radio 4 topical comedy show, but split after 'Now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plain synonyms: a noun for the current moment, and a verb for putting something on display.

clue.text: Ate garlic, transforming body tissue

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Eating garlic as if it could change your body.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ATE GARLIC rearrange into CARTILAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage is the firm, flexible connective tissue in joints, ears and nose.

clue.text: Revise setter's boring conclusion

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
the setter refers to themself as ME; 'setter's' is setter is

explanation.surface: An editor asking the setter to rewrite a dull ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, describing the conclusion, but it is the drilling kind: ME goes into END.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean correcting a text by editing it.

clue.text: Area covered by detective with additional clause in contract, one who must deliver

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector; the area covered is the DI's patch
a police officer's patch is the area they cover
a rider is a clause added to a contract or bill

explanation.surface: A detective's territory bound up in a contract with extra conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The area covered by a detective is the DI's PATCH, so the possessive 'S' comes from the detective. 'with' simply joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch rider carries messages or parcels, usually by motorbike, and must deliver them.

clue.text: Wise to follow universal convention

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the wise word is placed after the universal letter

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Advice that it is wise to go along with what everyone does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universal convention' reads as one phrase, but 'universal' gives only U and 'convention' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or practice, a convention.

clue.text: Bother about current head's tendency to be late

parts.note: 'Bother!' and 'Drat!' are both mild curses
I is the symbol for electric current
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Complaining about how often the current headteacher turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother about' looks like worry over something, but 'Bother' is the exclamation DRAT, turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the habit of arriving late.

clue.text: Emergence of insect from active colonies

indicators.note: the letters are lively and move about

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Insects pouring out of busy colonies, as from an ant nest.
explanation.walkthrough: An uncommon word, but the fodder is right there: COLONIES rearranges into ECLOSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclosion is an insect's emergence from its pupa case or egg.

clue.text: Surprisingly, it results in help for understanding opera?

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'results' is used twice over, as fodder and as the link

explanation.surface: A remark that something unexpectedly makes opera easier to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'it results': the IT and RESULTS letters rearrange into SURTITLES, with 'in' joining to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Surtitles are translated words projected above the stage so the audience can follow an opera.

clue.text: Collar robber that is hiding

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, starting after the first three letters of 'robber' and stopping before the final letter of 'that'

explanation.surface: A police instruction to collar a thief who is in hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a verb for arrest, fitting the robber, but it is the noun: a bertha.
explanation.definitionFit: A bertha is a wide, deep collar, often of lace, on a woman's dress.

clue.text: On reflection, somewhat wicked method to catch animals

indicators.note: a reflection is mirrored, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: somewhat is partly, in part
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: Musing that a way of catching animals seems a little cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' tempts a solver to hunt for a hidden word, but it simply gives PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A live trap catches an animal without harming it, a humane method of capture.

clue.text: Middle Easterner from Bahrain regularly after narcotic leaves

indicators.note: every other letter of 'Bahrain' is taken

parts.note: qat (khat) is a plant whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant drug
its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters

explanation.surface: A traveller from Bahrain after the narcotic has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like departs, but QAT is the name of the leaves themselves. 'narcotic leaves' is one definition of QAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Qatari is a person from Qatar, a Gulf state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Hospital stopping heart is relatively stupid

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A remark that a hospital letting a heart stop is rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' signals a comparative: THICKER is more stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick means stupid, so thicker is more stupid.

clue.text: Famous husband will run India with Conservative

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
'he is to go' means he will go
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A notable husband who will lead India alongside a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will run' reads as one verb, but 'will' is IS TO and 'run' is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means famous or important in history.

clue.text: Outrageously sexy rector with beer belly, perhaps going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: paunchy means having a big belly, such as a beer belly

explanation.surface: A scandalous image of a pot-bellied clergyman stripping off his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUNCHY 'going topless' drops its P, and R goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy means earthy and sexually explicit, so outrageously sexy.

clue.text: Cane puzzle with a third missing

indicators.note: a third of a nine-letter word is three letters, here the last three taken away

parts.note: to bamboozle someone is to puzzle or baffle them

explanation.surface: A setter's remark about a cane-themed puzzle with part of it absent.
explanation.walkthrough: BAMBOOZLE has nine letters; 'with a third missing' drops its final three.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is the hard, hollow-stemmed giant grass used for canes.

clue.text: Knock out European chasing bronze approximately 1600 metres back

indicators.note: the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a tan is a bronze colour on the skin
1 MILE is about 1,609 metres, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An athlete from Europe, trailing in bronze position over a mile, being knocked out of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole wordplay, not just the mile. The digit 1 becomes the letter I, a common setter's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: both mean removing a competitor from a contest.

clue.text: More conservative Britpop band covering Bowie at last

parts.note: Blur were a leading 1990s Britpop band

indicators.note: the letter that comes at last, at the very end, of Bowie's name

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A 1990s band doing a David Bowie cover in a rather more conservative style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' looks like a band's cover version of a song, but it means BLUR wraps round E. Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative party, so bluer means more conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative party colour, so bluer means more Tory.

clue.text: Easily close growing business losing millions

parts.note: close by is nearby
a farm is a business that grows crops; without M it is FAR
M is the abbreviation for millions; it is the letter lost

explanation.surface: A fast-growing company closing down easily after losing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing business' reads like an expanding company, but it is one that grows things: a FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: By far means easily or by a wide margin, as in easily the best.

clue.text: Peasant couple start to live

parts.note: to yoke is to couple, join together

indicators.note: the starting letter of 'live'

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A peasant pair setting up home together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' reads as a pair of people, but it is the verb: to YOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a peasant.

clue.text: Festival established for Spooner is outrageous

indicators.note: for Spooner means swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Rev. Spooner was said to do

parts.note: a fair is a festival, a word said exactly like fare
based means established or founded, as in a firm based in Leeds

explanation.surface: A newly founded festival is causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR BASED, with its first sounds swapped 'for Spooner', is heard as BARE FACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefaced means shameless and undisguised, as in a barefaced lie, so outrageous.

clue.text: Work of art liberated Celt, mostly

parts.note: free means liberated; the same 'mostly' that trims Scot also cuts free to its first three letters

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter, and here it serves both words

parts.note: a Scot is a Celt

explanation.surface: A painting showing a Celtic warrior set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' serves both words: FREE and SCOT each lose their last letter, giving FRE and SCO, joined in the order printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting done on wet plaster, a work of art on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: An enthralling cultured raver?

parts.note: 'an' means per, as in five pounds an hour
arty means interested in the arts, cultured

explanation.surface: A cultivated person enjoying a rave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' is the small word most easily overlooked; here it means PER. 'enthralling' looks like praise, but it holds ARTY captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A partyer is someone who goes to parties, a raver.
